memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If anyone sins because they do not speak up when they hear a public charge to testify regarding something they have seen or learned about, they will be held responsible.'" - Lev 5:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter opens with a sin of silence.

A public appeal has gone out. Someone knows something — they saw it, or they heard it. And they say nothing. Perhaps to avoid trouble. Perhaps to protect a friend. Perhaps because speaking would cost them something.

God calls that sin.

We rarely think this way. We assume guilt requires an action, and that staying out of it keeps our hands clean. But Scripture consistently holds us responsible for what we knew and did not say. If you fail to act in a situation that requires moral courage, you have acted.

This is not a licence to become the person who comments on everything. There is a real biblical warning about the loose tongue too. The issue here is specific: withholding truth that justice needs.

Jesus called His followers salt and light (Mtt 5:13-16) — both of which work by being present, not hidden. James writes that if anyone knows the good they ought to do and doesn't do it, it is sin for them (Jas 4:17).

Is there something you know that someone needs to hear? A truth being denied, a wrong being covered, a person being blamed unfairly? Silence is not always neutral.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I stayed silent when I should have spoken?
2. What has silence been costing me — or costing someone else?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I kept quiet to keep myself comfortable. Give me courage to speak the truth where it is needed. Amen.
